q: אישה בת 83 מאושפזת, ובנה הוא אפוטרופוס שמונה לה. עולה חשד שניצל את כספה ופעל בניגוד לטובתה. הצוות מערב עובד סוציאלי ופועל להגנתה ולדיווח כנדרש. איזה גורם מוסמך לפטר את האפוטרופוס בשל מילוי לקוי של תפקידו?
o: מנהל בית החולים לאחר בירור התנהלות האפוטרופוס
בית המשפט לאחר בירור התנהלות האפוטרופוס
פסיכיאטר מומחה לאחר בירור התנהלות האפוטרופוס
עובד סוציאלי לאחר בירור התנהלות האפוטרופוס
explanation:
**פיטורי אפוטרופוס** בשל מילוי לקוי של תפקידו הם בסמכות **בית המשפט** לפי סעיף 61. במקביל, חשד להתעמרות מחייב פעולה של הצוות הרפואי והסוציאלי להגנה ולבירור; פעולות אלה אינן כשלעצמן פיטורים של אפוטרופוס שמונה. אין צורך להכריע בשאלת הפיטורים כדי להתחיל להגן על המטופלת (חוק הכשרות, עמ׳ 57; נוהל ההתעמרות, עמ׳ 6; המשפט האחרון הוא יישום של סדר הפעולות בנוהל).
"בית המשפט רשאי לפטר אפוטרופוס אם לא מילא תפקידיו כראוי או אם ראה בית המשפט סיבה אחרת לפיטוריו." (עמ׳ 57).

**א. מנהל בית החולים לאחר בירור התנהלות האפוטרופוס.** שגויה, סמכות הפיטורים שבסעיף 61 היא של בית המשפט. הבירור בבית החולים אינו משנה את זהות הגורם המוסמך (חוק הכשרות, עמ׳ 57).
**ב. בית המשפט לאחר בירור התנהלות האפוטרופוס.** נכונה, הסעיף מסמיך את בית המשפט לפטר אפוטרופוס שלא מילא את תפקידיו כראוי, או כשקיימת סיבה אחרת לפיטוריו (חוק הכשרות, עמ׳ 57).
**ג. פסיכיאטר מומחה לאחר בירור התנהלות האפוטרופוס.** שגויה, מומחיות רפואית אינה סמכות שיפוטית לפטר אפוטרופוס. הסעיף מקנה את סמכות הפיטורים לבית המשפט (חוק הכשרות, עמ׳ 57).
**ד. עובד סוציאלי לאחר בירור התנהלות האפוטרופוס.** שגויה, לעובד הסוציאלי תפקיד מיידי בבירור החשד ובהערכת הסיכון, אך פיטורי האפוטרופוס נעשים בידי בית המשפט (נוהל ההתעמרות, עמ׳ 6; חוק הכשרות, עמ׳ 57).

מקור: חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, תשכ״ב־1962, סעיף 61, עמ׳ PDF 57; נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, סעיף 8, עמ׳ 6.

q: An older patient with glaucoma has difficulty avoiding obstacles while walking. Which characteristic change explains this difficulty?
o: Optic disk damage with loss of peripheral visual fields
Lens clouding with scattering of light within the eye
Macular damage with loss of central visual fields
Posterior brain injury with loss of half the visual field
explanation:
**Glaucoma-related peripheral field loss** can interfere with safe walking because objects outside the remaining field may not be seen. Hazzard states: "The effect of peripheral field loss on daily life is most problematic in safe ambulation." (p. 474).

**A. Optic disk damage with loss of peripheral visual fields.** Correct, glaucoma can damage the optic disk and peripheral visual fields, explaining collisions with unseen obstacles (p. 474).
**B. Lens clouding with scattering of light within the eye.** Wrong, this does not describe the optic disk and peripheral-field damage through which the source explains this glaucoma-related difficulty (p. 474).
**C. Macular damage with loss of central visual fields.** Wrong, the relevant loss in the glaucoma passage is peripheral, not a central-field defect attributed to the macula (p. 474).
**D. Posterior brain injury with loss of half the visual field.** Wrong, the source explains this difficulty through glaucoma-related peripheral field loss, rather than a half-field defect from brain injury (p. 474).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 474.
ref: Hazzard Ch 33 — LOW VISION: ASSESSMENT AND REHABILITATION

q: A 70-year-old woman with heart failure, diabetes, and arthritis reports that her medications are affecting sexual function. She takes metoprolol, furosemide, metformin, and gabapentin for neuropathic pain and asks about changing treatment. Which approach best reflects the source's discussion of medication-related sexual concerns in older women?
o: Stop metoprolol on the assumption that its class explains the sexual problem
Change the diuretic on the assumption that this will restore sexual function
Review medications alongside disease control and other contributors to sexual function
Attribute the problem to age and defer assessment of treatment-related contributors
explanation:
**Sexual-function assessment** requires attention to medical, psychological, social, and treatment-related contributors. Evidence for specific medication effects in older women is limited, and treatment benefits may offset sexual adverse effects; this favors an individualized review rather than assuming a drug cause (pp. 518, 521).
"Evidence for the effects of drugs on sexual dysfunction is mixed overall and very limited with respect to older females, specifically." (p. 518).

**A. Stop metoprolol on the assumption that its class explains the sexual problem.** Wrong, the source says no antihypertensive class is consistently associated with female sexual dysfunction, so this attribution is not established (p. 521).
**B. Change the diuretic on the assumption that this will restore sexual function.** Wrong, the same evidence limitation does not support predicting restoration of sexual function from an empirical diuretic switch (pp. 518, 521).
**C. Review medications alongside disease control and other contributors to sexual function.** Correct, this considers the multiple contributors and the balance between disease treatment and possible adverse effects (p. 518).
**D. Attribute the problem to age and defer assessment of treatment-related contributors.** Wrong, the source describes potentially addressable medical and treatment-related contributors, so age alone does not replace assessment (p. 518).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 518, 521.
ref: Hazzard Ch 35 — SEXUALITY, SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING WOMAN
chapterTitle: Sexuality, Sexual Function, and the Aging Woman

q: When discussing prognosis after colon cancer surgery, Hazzard describes a surgical cohort in which cardiovascular disease was the next most frequent cause of death after colorectal cancer. What implication follows for counseling an older patient?
o: Reduce the importance assigned to comorbid disease when planning follow-up
Consider deaths from comorbid disease alongside deaths from colorectal cancer
Give another primary cancer greater prognostic weight than cardiovascular disease
Infer that cardiovascular death is more frequent than death from the original cancer
explanation:
**Competing causes of death** matter when interpreting survival after cancer surgery. In the reported cohort, Hazzard lists "cardiovascular disease (24.5%) and another primary cancer (7.4%)" after colorectal cancer among causes of death (p. 1440). Inference: counseling should therefore consider comorbid disease alongside the original cancer, without treating cohort proportions as a personal forecast.

**A. Reduce the importance assigned to comorbid disease when planning follow-up.** Wrong, this inference goes against the substantial contribution of cardiovascular disease described among deaths in the cohort (p. 1440).
**B. Consider deaths from comorbid disease alongside deaths from colorectal cancer.** Correct, this is the supported counseling inference: the cohort includes deaths from both colorectal cancer and comorbid cardiovascular disease (p. 1440).
**C. Give another primary cancer greater prognostic weight than cardiovascular disease.** Wrong, the reported ordering places cardiovascular disease ahead of another primary cancer, not below it (p. 1440).
**D. Infer that cardiovascular death is more frequent than death from the original cancer.** Wrong, the source places colorectal cancer ahead of cardiovascular disease in this cohort; it does not support that reversal (p. 1440).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1440.

q: In the PACIFIC trial described in Hazzard, at what point in the treatment of unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer was durvalumab given?
o: Before starting concurrent chemotherapy and radiation therapy
After progression during concurrent chemotherapy and radiation therapy
After disease control with concurrent chemoradiation
After surgical resection without preceding radiation therapy
explanation:
**Durvalumab in PACIFIC** was studied after concurrent chemoradiation had achieved disease control in unresectable stage III NSCLC. The sequence and disease-control requirement distinguish this setting from treatment before chemoradiation, treatment after progression, or postoperative treatment (p. 1426). "In the PACIFIC trial, 713 patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who had disease control after concurrent chemoradiation were randomized 2 to 1 to durvalumab" (p. 1426).

**A. Before starting concurrent chemotherapy and radiation therapy.** Wrong, the trial described treatment after concurrent chemoradiation had achieved disease control, not before that treatment began (p. 1426).
**B. After progression during concurrent chemotherapy and radiation therapy.** Wrong, patients had disease control after chemoradiation; progression during it does not match that entry condition (p. 1426).
**C. After disease control with concurrent chemoradiation.** Correct, this matches both the preceding treatment and the disease-control condition specified in the trial (p. 1426).
**D. After surgical resection without preceding radiation therapy.** Wrong, the described population had unresectable disease and prior concurrent chemoradiation, not surgery without radiation (p. 1426).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1426.

q: אישה בת 70 עם מספר מחלות כרוניות שואלת את הגריאטר שלה לגבי תכנון לנכות עתידית אפשרית. בעלה נפטר לפני 5 שנים והיא גרה לבד. היא חוששת מהמשמעויות הכלכליות של צורך אפשרי בטיפול ארוך-טווח. איזה היבט של דפוסי אריכות החיים בנשים משפיע באופן הישיר ביותר על צרכי תכנון הטיפול שלה?
o: לנשים יש עלויות בריאות נמוכות יותר לאורך החיים בשל תחזוקת בריאות טובה יותר
תוחלת החיים הארוכה יותר של נשים כוללת לעיתים קרובות תקופות ממושכות של ירידה תפקודית ואלמנות
נשים מסתגלות טוב יותר לסביבות של assisted living
לנשים יש רשתות תמיכה משפחתיות חזקות יותר
explanation:
התשובה היא **אפשרות לשנים ממושכות של מוגבלות ואלמנות**. נשים נוטות לשרוד אחרי בני זוגן, ובמקביל נושאות יותר מגבלות תפקודיות; לכן תכנון טיפול ותמיכה עשוי להידרש לאורך זמן (עמ׳ 27, 92).

**א. לנשים יש עלויות בריאות נמוכות יותר לאורך החיים בשל תחזוקת בריאות טובה יותר.** שגויה, אין להסיק עלויות נמוכות מיתרון ההישרדות. הספר מתאר יותר ביקורי רופא, ימי אשפוז, תרופות ומגבלות אצל נשים, המצדיקים תכנון משאבים אישי (עמ׳ 92; יישום לתכנון).
**ב. תוחלת החיים הארוכה יותר של נשים כוללת לעיתים קרובות תקופות ממושכות של ירידה תפקודית ואלמנות.** נכונה, נשים נוטות יותר להתאלמן עקב תוחלת חיים ארוכה יותר. מוגבלות, מחלות כרוניות וחיים ללא בן זוג עלולים להאריך את הצורך בעזרה; נשים גם מיוצגות ביתר במסגרות מגורים טיפוליות. יש לתכנן תמיכה זמינה, יכולת מימון, רצונות עתידיים ושמירת עצמאות, במיוחד לאלמנה עם מחלות כרוניות (עמ׳ 27, 92; יישום לתרחיש).
**ג. נשים מסתגלות טוב יותר לסביבות של assisted living.** שגויה, הסתגלות לדיור מוגן אינה מסבירה את הצורך לתכנן שנות תמיכה ממושכות, ואין במקור בסיס להניח הסתגלות טובה יותר למטופלת זו (עמ׳ 27, 92).
**ד. לנשים יש רשתות תמיכה משפחתיות חזקות יותר.** שגויה, אי אפשר להניח שרשת משפחתית מספיקה תישאר זמינה. המקור מציג אלמנות ומצב כלכלי ובריאותי כגורמים בצורת המגורים, ומדגיש התייחסות למטפל ולמשפחה בתכנון (עמ׳ 27).

מקור: Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 27, 92.

q: A 79-year-old former boxer develops behavioral and cognitive changes. His family asks how chronic traumatic encephalopathy is definitively diagnosed according to Hazzard. Which type of evidence supports the definitive diagnosis described in the source?
o: Neuropathologic examination demonstrating the characteristic pattern of tau pathology
PET imaging demonstrating a characteristic pattern of tau uptake
Cerebrospinal fluid testing demonstrating a characteristic tau-to-amyloid ratio
Cognitive testing demonstrating a characteristic pattern of cognitive deficits
explanation:
**Chronic traumatic encephalopathy** is defined neuropathologically in the source: "Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is diagnosed neuropathologically and is a primary tauopathy with a distinct well-defined pattern of tau pathology" (p. 997). Its clinical presentations are nonspecific, and the source does not regard imaging, laboratory, or cognitive tests as definitive during life (p. 997).

**A. Neuropathologic examination demonstrating the characteristic pattern of tau pathology.** Correct, the source bases diagnosis on the characteristic neuropathologic tau pattern. Behavioral and cognitive symptoms do not substitute for this evidence (p. 997).
**B. PET imaging demonstrating a characteristic pattern of tau uptake.** Wrong, PET is neuroimaging; the source explicitly states that neuroimaging does not provide a definitive diagnosis during life. A proposed uptake pattern does not meet its stated standard (p. 997).
**C. Cerebrospinal fluid testing demonstrating a characteristic tau-to-amyloid ratio.** Wrong, this is laboratory evidence, which the source explicitly does not accept as definitive during life. It is not the neuropathologic demonstration asked for (p. 997).
**D. Cognitive testing demonstrating a characteristic pattern of cognitive deficits.** Wrong, the source describes nonspecific clinical presentations and explicitly excludes cognitive tests as a definitive diagnostic method during life (p. 997).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 997.
ref: Hazzard Ch 64 — TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY AND CHRONIC TRAUMATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY
chapterTitle: TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY AND CHRONIC TRAUMATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY

q: An 82-year-old woman with dementia sometimes refuses tablets. After the team adjusts medication administration, she willingly accepts oral treatment. Persistent hypertension requires treatment; a thiazide previously caused hyponatremia, and there is no cardiac indication for a beta-blocker. Renal function and potassium are normal. Which class is the most appropriate initial choice among these options according to Hazzard?
o: A centrally acting antihypertensive such as clonidine
An ACE inhibitor such as lisinopril
A beta-blocker such as metoprolol
A direct vasodilator such as hydralazine
explanation:
**ACE inhibitors** are an initial-treatment option in older adults. The source favors drugs with fewer adverse effects and advises avoiding centrally acting agents and direct vasodilators because of sedation and marked postural hypotension, respectively; beta-blockers are not a first-line choice without a compelling indication (p. 1225).
"ACE inhibitor agents and angiotensin receptor blockers are choices for initial therapy or as second agents in combination with a thiazide-type diuretic." (p. 1225).
"centrally acting antihypertensive medications and direct vasodilators are best avoided in older hypertensive patients" (p. 1225).

**A. A centrally acting antihypertensive such as clonidine.** Wrong, centrally acting drugs are best avoided because of central nervous system sedating effects, making this an unfavorable initial class here (p. 1225).
**B. An ACE inhibitor such as lisinopril.** Correct, this is a listed initial-treatment class; its favorable adverse-effect profile supports its selection among the choices when a thiazide is unsuitable (p. 1225).
**C. A beta-blocker such as metoprolol.** Wrong, the stem supplies no compelling indication, the condition the source requires for choosing this class first in older patients (p. 1225).
**D. A direct vasodilator such as hydralazine.** Wrong, direct vasodilators are associated with marked postural hypotension and are best avoided as a general initial choice in older patients (p. 1225).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1225.

q: בן 86, בריא בדרך כלל, שמור קוגניטיבית. לא היה אצל רופאת המשפחה ב- 5 השנים האחרונות ולא עשה בדיקות דם. הגיע למחלקה לרפואה דחופה (חדר מיון) לאחר נפילה ברחוב. בדיקה גופנית ללא ממצא משמעותי. לחץ הדם שמור, ללא חום. בדיקה גופנית תקינה ואין עדות לשבר או חבלת ראש. בספירת הדם: מדד ויחידות המטופל ערכים תקינים WBC 10e3qµL 31.2 4.0-11.0 HgB gr/dl 14.5 17 - 13.2 PLT 10e3qµL 231 140-450 NEU % 11 40-75 LYM % 85 20-40 במשטח דם: המטופל מתמצא בסיטואציה, במקום ובזמן, ללא חסר קוגניטיבי בולט ומעוניין להשתחרר לביתו. מה ההמלצה הטיפולית לגבי הממצא בספירת הדם?
o: אשפוז עם טיפול אנטיביוטי רחב טווח בחשד ל- SEPSIS
אשפוז לצורך בדיקת מח עצם בחשד ל- ACUTE LEUKEMIA
שחרור למעקב מרפאה המטולוגית בחשד ל- CHRONIC LYMPHOCYTIC LEUKEMIA
שחרור עם המלצה לטיפול ב- G-CSF עקב נויטרופניה אסימפטומטית ומעקב מרפאה המטולוגית בהקדם
explanation:
The stem describes **absolute lymphocytosis without anemia or thrombocytopenia**, raising suspicion for CLL. Diagnosis requires demonstration of a monoclonal B-cell population by flow-cytometric immunophenotyping. CLL is the most common leukemia in the Western Hemisphere and may be detected as asymptomatic lymphocytosis; early asymptomatic disease calls for observation rather than immediate treatment (Hazzard 8e, pp. 1490-1491).

**A. Admit for broad-spectrum antibiotics for suspected sepsis.** Wrong, the stem describes no fever, instability, or infection-directed symptoms. As an inference from the case and asymptomatic CLL presentation, the high cell count alone does not justify sepsis treatment; this does not generally exclude infection in CLL (p. 1490).
**B. Admit for bone marrow examination for suspected acute leukemia.** Wrong, initial assessment of suspected CLL can use peripheral blood and flow cytometry; bone marrow studies are usually unnecessary for diagnosis. Lymphocytosis alone does not establish a need for admission for marrow examination for acute leukemia (p. 1490).
**C. Discharge for hematology follow-up for suspected chronic lymphocytic leukemia.** Correct, for scoring and consistent with the described stable condition. Hematology follow-up permits diagnostic confirmation and staging. This is a clinical inference from observation in early asymptomatic CLL; the blood count alone does not establish the final stage (pp. 1490-1491).
**D. Discharge with G-CSF for asymptomatic neutropenia and prompt hematology follow-up.** Wrong, the neutrophil percentage is relatively low in the setting of lymphocytosis; the data do not imply a low absolute count. Calculating an absolute count applies the stem's data. The source-directed investigation is peripheral-blood assessment for CLL, not colony-stimulating treatment based on the neutrophil percentage alone (p. 1490).

CLL may be found incidentally, and its diagnosis alone does not require immediate treatment; decisions depend on stage and symptoms (pp. 1490-1491).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1490-1491.

q: בת 74, א-סימפטומטית, עשתה בדיקות דם שגרתיות. עקב שקיעת דם מוחשת נמצא חלבון מונוקלונלי IgG קאפא. כיצד ניתן לאבחן שמדובר ב- MGUS ( MONOCLONAL GAMMOPATHY OF UNCERTAIN SIGNIFICANCE ) ולא ב- MULTOPLE MYELOMA?
o: ב- MGUS יש חלבון מונוקלונלי IgG פחות מ- 30 גרם/ליטר
ב- MGUS יש פחות מ- 30% תאי פלסמה במח העצם
ב- MGUS ההמוגלובין בסביבות 10
ב- MGUS אין חלבון מונוקלונלי בשתן
explanation:
**MGUS** includes a serum monoclonal protein below 30 g/L. This concentration alone is insufficient: the remaining marrow and end-organ criteria must also be satisfied (pp. 1501–1503).

**A. In MGUS, monoclonal IgG is below 30 g/L.** Correct, this fits the serum criterion for non-IgM MGUS. Low marrow plasma-cell burden and absence of attributable organ damage must also be confirmed (p. 1502).
**B. In MGUS, marrow plasma cells are below 30%.** Wrong, the requirement is below 10%; the proposed threshold permits too high a burden to distinguish MGUS properly from more advanced disease (p. 1502).
**C. In MGUS, hemoglobin is around 10.** Wrong, anemia attributable to the plasma-cell disorder constitutes end-organ damage rather than confirming MGUS; its cause needs investigation (p. 1502).
**D. In MGUS, no monoclonal protein is present in urine.** Wrong, the table’s IgG MGUS definition rests on serum protein, marrow plasma cells and absence of attributable damage. Absence of urinary protein cannot replace those requirements (p. 1502).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1501, 1502, 1503.

q: בת 60 מגיעה למרפאה בליווי בעלה. הבעל מתאר כי במהלך חצי השנה האחרונה נצפו שינויים התנהגותיים, הכוללים אכילה ללא שליטה של ממתקים, הערות פוגעניות כלפי זרים, בפעם אחרונה שהגיעה לביקור אצל חברים נכנסה לחדר השינה שלהם. והחלה לפתוח מגירות ללא מחלות רקע. בדיקה גופנית תקינה. ללא מחשבות שווא או הלוסינציות. מינימנטל 28/30, במבחן שעון סימנה נכון את המספרים אבל לא הצליחה לסמן את השעה עם. המחוגים מהו הממצא הפתולוגי המאפיין את מצבה של המטופלת?
o: משקעי בתא עמילואיד ו- TAU
משקעי TAU
משקעי Alpha-synuclein
משקעי בתא עמילואיד
explanation:
The presentation suggests **behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia**: behavioral and executive changes may occur with relatively preserved memory. **FTLD is pathologically heterogeneous**, so the clinical syndrome alone cannot identify the protein, although tau is the officially accepted choice among these options (pp. 873, 899).

**A. Beta-amyloid and tau deposits.** Wrong, this combination characterizes Alzheimer pathology. The behavioral and executive presentation points toward FTLD, without absolutely excluding alternatives on the basis of age or a single test (pp. 873, 898-899).
**B. Tau deposits.** Correct, according to the official key, because tau is among the proteins implicated in FTLD. The syndrome alone does not establish that every such case is a tauopathy (pp. 873, 899).
**C. Alpha-synuclein deposits.** Wrong, alpha-synuclein is the central protein in Lewy bodies. The source describes cognitive fluctuations, parkinsonian features, and hallucinations in that context, rather than this isolated frontal pattern (pp. 870, 873).
**D. Beta-amyloid deposits.** Wrong, amyloid is not the pathological explanation toward which this FTLD syndrome points; FTLD includes tau or TDP-43 inclusions, among others (p. 873).

Pathologically, FTLD is heterogeneous and includes tau or TDP-43 deposits, among others; tau fits best among the offered answers (p. 873). Tau pathology occurs in Pick disease, corticobasal degeneration, and progressive supranuclear palsy (p. 899). FTLD involves frontal and temporal regions and is a common cause of dementia in middle age, below age 65; the behavioral syndrome alone cannot establish tau pathology (p. 873).

Source versus explanation: "progressive supranuclear palsy, corticobasal degeneration, and Pick disease" (p. 899). The inherited Hebrew passage garbled the names of progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration; the correct source terms are used here.

MMSE performance may remain normal early in FTD, so the behavioral history matters even when memory screening is relatively preserved. Disinhibition, overeating, and executive difficulty on clock drawing suggest bvFTD; they do not identify its pathological protein (p. 873).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 870, 873, 898-899.
referenceNote: Paper cites chapters 57,63 and pp.873,933. Table 63-5 is on p.993 (chapter 63); p.933 is a bibliography page. Open page uses pp.873 and 993.

q: An 80-year-old woman with a painful vertebral compression fracture that has not responded to conservative treatment is referred for consideration of vertebroplasty or kyphoplasty. Which description matches the indication presented in Hazzard rather than a contraindication?
o: A compression fracture with active, uncorrected coagulopathy
An acutely painful compression fracture with persistent pain
A burst fracture with bone retropulsed into the spinal canal
A fracture with loss of more than 66% of vertebral height
explanation:
**Vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty** are described as procedures used for persistently painful acute vertebral compression fractures. Hazzard separately lists coagulopathy, burst fractures with retropulsed bone, and vertebral height loss greater than 66% as contraindications (p. 1066). "Two minimally invasive procedures, vertebroplasty (VP) and kyphoplasty (KP), are commonly used to treat persistent, acutely painful VCFs." (p. 1066).

**A. A compression fracture with active, uncorrected coagulopathy.** Wrong, existing coagulopathy is a listed contraindication, so this finding does not identify the source’s treatment indication (p. 1066).
**B. An acutely painful compression fracture with persistent pain.** Correct, persistent pain in an acutely painful compression fracture matches the clinical use described (p. 1066).
**C. A burst fracture with bone retropulsed into the spinal canal.** Wrong, a burst fracture with retropulsed bone is explicitly listed as a contraindication (p. 1066).
**D. A fracture with loss of more than 66% of vertebral height.** Wrong, height loss greater than 66% is explicitly listed as a contraindication (p. 1066).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1066.

q: בת 78, התקבלה למחלקת שיקום לאחר אשפוז עקב אירוע מוחי עם שיתוק בפלג גוף ימין. בבדיקתה פצע לחץ דרגה 3 בעכוז. איזו מההתערבויות הבאות הוכחה כמשפרת ריפוי של פצע הלחץ באופן משמעותי?
o: שימוש במזרון דינמי
טיפול בחמצן היפרבארי
תוספת טיפול בוויטמינים A,E,C IRON
אנטיביוטיקה סיסטמית
explanation:
Official answer: א

**Pressure off-loading** is fundamental in treating a stage 3 pressure injury, and a dynamic mattress is a pressure-redistributing surface. Page 698 supports off-loading and support surfaces but does not establish a significant healing effect from a dynamic mattress alone (pp. 684, 698).

**A. A dynamic mattress.** Correct, accepted for scoring. The source includes pressure-redistributing surfaces and evidence of healing support from specialized beds for deep injuries. The limitation concerning a dynamic mattress alone remains (pp. 692, 698).
**B. Hyperbaric oxygen.** Wrong, this is discussed for selected settings such as refractory osteomyelitis or a threatened flap, neither described here (p. 695).
**C. Vitamins A, E, C and iron.** Wrong, evidence does not support these supplements for healing without a specific deficiency, which was not supplied (p. 692).
**D. Systemic antibiotics.** Wrong, these are used for infection such as osteomyelitis. Injury stage alone does not establish infection or justify antibiotics as the healing intervention here (p. 695).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 684, 692, 695, 698.

q: בן 65, שוקל 80 קילו, אובחן עם תסמונת Guillain-Barré לאחר שהתייצג עם חולשה סימטרית עולה וא-רפלקסיה. לאחר 5 ימי טיפול ב IVIg-במינון 160 גרם ליום, לא נצפה שיפור משמעותי במצבו. מה ההחלטה הטיפולית הנכונה כעת?
o: להתחיל טיפול משולב של IVIg עם פלזמפרזיס להגברת יעילות הטיפול
להחליף את הטיפול לפלזמפרזיס מכיוון שה- IVIg לא היה יעיל
להמשיך מעקב ותמיכה נשימתית בהתאם לצורך, ללא שינוי בטיפול האימונומודולטורי
לתת מחזור נוסף של IVIg במינון גבוה יותר
explanation:
Official answer: ג

**Lack of early improvement** does not establish treatment failure in Guillain–Barré syndrome. Continue respiratory, swallowing and autonomic monitoring while recovery develops; early nonresponse alone does not justify automatically changing immunotherapy (Leonhard 2019, steps 6 and 8).

**A. Combine IVIg with plasma exchange for greater efficacy.** Wrong, routine sequential combination is not more effective than either treatment alone and adds treatment burden (van Doorn 2023, pp. 3661–3662).
**B. Switch to plasma exchange because IVIg was ineffective.** Wrong, routine switching after nonresponse lacks trial support; exchange immediately after IVIg also removes the infused immunoglobulin (van Doorn, pp. 3661–3662).
**C. Continue monitoring and respiratory support as needed without changing immunomodulation.** Correct, active support protects against complications while recovery evolves; the stem does not supply a reason for another immunomodulatory course (Leonhard, steps 6 and 8; van Doorn, pp. 3661–3662).
**D. Give another higher-dose IVIg course.** Wrong, the guideline favors the standard course; an additional course in poor-prognosis patients did not improve outcomes and caused more severe adverse effects (van Doorn, p. 3661).

Note: The official stem contains a dose error. A standard course totals 2 g/kg over 5 days: for 80 kg, 160 g in total, approximately 32 g/day, not 160 g/day. This is arithmetic from 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (Leonhard, step 5; van Doorn, p. 3661).
Inherited source note: Harrison 22e p. 3620 and official 2025 paper p. 13 were the historical citations for this correction. The original note states that combined IVIg and plasma exchange was not significantly more effective than either alone and that the cited Harrison page did not justify attribution to the ICE trial. Those historical pages were not rechecked here; the dose and combination-treatment points were independently verified in the articles above.

Source: Leonhard SE et al. Nat Rev Neurol. 2019;15:671–683, steps 5–8, doi:10.1038/s41582-019-0250-9; van Doorn PA et al. Eur J Neurol. 2023;30:3646–3674, pp. 3661–3662, doi:10.1111/ene.16073.

q: What agent inhibits the activity of collagenase during enzymatic debridement?
o: Endogenous proteolytic enzymes
Collagen wound dressings
Disinfected fly larvae
Topically applied iodine
explanation:
**Iodine inhibits collagenase**, making this combination relevant when selecting materials for enzymatic debridement. Hazzard states that "iodine inhibits the activity of collagenase." (p. 696). Collagenase is applied to degrade necrotic tissue, so an inhibitor works against the intended enzymatic action (p. 696; inference from the described mechanism).

**A. Endogenous proteolytic enzymes.** Wrong, the chapter describes endogenous proteolytic enzymes as digesting nonviable tissue during autolytic debridement, not as the agent inhibiting collagenase in the stated interaction (p. 696).
**B. Collagen wound dressings.** Wrong, collagen dressings are described as lowering elastase in chronic wounds and supporting healing; this is distinct from inhibition of the collagenase ointment (p. 696).
**C. Disinfected fly larvae.** Wrong, disinfected fly larvae provide biosurgical debridement. This is a tissue-removal method, not the collagenase-inhibiting agent identified in the enzymatic-debridement section (p. 696).
**D. Topically applied iodine.** Correct, the enzymatic-debridement section specifically identifies iodine as inhibiting collagenase activity; dressing compatibility therefore matters when this ointment is used (p. 696).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, pp. 696.

q: Why was the Clinical Frailty Scale developed as a practical alternative to the detailed Frailty Index in the approach described by Hazzard?
o: It uses the clinician’s overall impression to make frailty assessment simpler in clinical practice.
It requires collection of the same large variable set before a clinical impression can be used.
It confines assessment to physical deficits by excluding cognitive impairment, disability and comorbidity.
It simplifies assessment by giving up the ability to predict institutionalization and death.
explanation:
The **Clinical Frailty Scale provides a simpler clinical assessment** based on the clinician’s overall impression. It was developed because the many variables needed for the Frailty Index make that approach unwieldy in clinical use, while the CFS retains similar predictive power for institutionalization and death (p. 623).
"developed a much simpler approach, the seven-category Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), based on the clinician’s overall impression." (p. 623).
"The CFS has similar predictive power to FI for institutionalization and death." (p. 623).

**A. It uses the clinician’s overall impression to make frailty assessment simpler in clinical practice.** Correct, an overall clinical impression is the basis of the simpler CFS approach, avoiding collection of the full Frailty Index variable set (p. 623).
**B. It requires collection of the same large variable set before a clinical impression can be used.** Wrong, the large variable burden is the practical problem the simpler CFS was intended to address, rather than a requirement it preserves (p. 623).
**C. It confines assessment to physical deficits by excluding cognitive impairment, disability and comorbidity.** Wrong, the source explicitly says that the CFS mixes comorbidity, cognitive impairment and disability; restricting it to physical deficits would misrepresent it (p. 623).
**D. It simplifies assessment by giving up the ability to predict institutionalization and death.** Wrong, the CFS has predictive power similar to the FI for institutionalization and death, so loss of prognostic usefulness is not its defining tradeoff (p. 623).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 623.

q: What is the recommended first-line treatment for insomnia in all adults, including older patients?
o: CBT-I
Temazepam
Flurazepam
Zolpidem
explanation:
CBT-I is recommended as first-line treatment for all adult insomnia (p659).

B. Temazepam: Pharmacotherapy is considered for acute triggers or persistence despite behavioral treatment; benzodiazepines are potentially inappropriate in older adults (p659).
D. Zolpidem: This hypnotic is discussed as pharmacotherapy with falls/confusion/fracture concerns; CBT-I is the stated first-line treatment (p659).
C. Flurazepam: The chapter says this long-acting benzodiazepine should not be used in older adults because of next-day effects (p659).
